# Health endpoint reference

This reference describes the `GET /health` request and response for the Boundary controller and worker. For an overview, refer to [Boundary health endpoints](/boundary/docs/monitor/health). For usage examples, refer to [Check the health endpoint](/boundary/docs/monitor/check-health-endpoint).

## Controller status codes

The controller health service exposes a single read-only endpoint. `GET /health` does not accept any input on the controller. All controller responses return empty bodies.

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | The api gRPC server of the controller is up. |
| `5xx` | The controller is unhealthy. A request timeout also indicates an unhealthy controller. |
| `503` | The controller is shutting down. |

## Worker requests

The worker health service uses the same path and accepts the `worker_info` query parameter.

| Request | Response |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /health` | Returns `200 OK` with an empty JSON object, `{}`. |
| `GET /health?worker_info=1` | Returns `200 OK` with a `worker_process_info` object. |

When a single Boundary instance runs both a controller and a worker, send `worker_info=1` to the controller endpoint to retrieve the worker information.

## Worker response fields

The `worker_process_info` object contains the following fields. Boundary omits fields that have a zero value from the response.

- `state` - The operational state of the worker. Possible values are `active`, `shutdown`, and `unknown`.

- `active_session_count` - The number of active sessions on the worker.

- `session_connections` - A map of session IDs to the number of open connections for each session. Boundary omits this field when the worker has no active connections.

- `upstream_connection_state` - The connection state of the worker to its upstream. Refer to [Upstream connection states](#upstream-connection-states) for the possible values.

### Upstream connection states

- `CONNECTING` - The channel is trying to make a connection and is waiting for name resolution or connection establishment.

- `READY` - The channel has successfully established a connection and communication has succeeded.

- `TRANSIENT_FAILURE` - The channel suffered a transient failure such as a timeout or socket error. The channel switches to `CONNECTING` and retries.

- `IDLE` - The channel is not attempting to create a connection because there are no calls.

- `SHUTDOWN` - The channel is shutting down. New calls fail immediately. Pending calls may continue until Boundary cancels them.

## Controller configuration parameter

- `graceful_shutdown_wait_duration` `(string: "")` - Specifies how long the controller waits before starting the shutdown process after receiving a shutdown signal. During this time, the health endpoint returns `503 Service Unavailable`. Set this parameter in the `controller` block of the configuration file. The value must be a duration string parseable by [ParseDuration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration), such as `"10s"`. The grace period is disabled when this parameter is not set.
